topic: Zoro had to lose to Mihawk to be able to cut a Knight of God
title: Zoro Had To Lose To Mihawk To Beat Sommers
description: Chapter 1194 only works because Zoro lost at the Baratie. Mihawk's lesson, Kuraigana and a regenerating Knight of God all connect. Is it a coincidence or Oda's plan?
comment: Was Zoro's loss at the Baratie the most important fight of his life, or was it Kuraigana? Pick one.

lines.text: Zoro had to lose to Mihawk to beat a Knight of God.

shot.search: Zoro Mihawk Sommers Supreme King Haki
shot.fallback: green haired swordsman with glowing black aura

lines.text: Hear me out, because chapter 1194 makes this weirdly literal.
Sommers notices Zoro can't fully control his Conqueror's Haki yet.

shot.fallback: knight healing from a deep cut

lines.text: So Zoro thinks back to Mihawk and his lesson about that Haki.

shot.fallback: hawk eyed swordsman instructing a student

lines.text: I think the lesson is control: stop pouring Haki out and aim it through the blades.

shot.search: Zoro three swords Supreme King Haki
shot.fallback: swordsman coating blades in black lightning

lines.text: Three swords coated, and the Haki finally flows through all of them.

shot.fallback: giant slash through an armored knight
swordsman falling on a ship deck

lines.text: Mihawk cuts Zoro down, and Zoro promises Luffy he'll never lose again until he beats him.

shot.fallback: swordsman bleeding, a boy in a straw hat watching

lines.text: No loss, no Kuraigana, no two years with Mihawk, and no lesson.

shot.fallback: two swordsmen training on a misty island

lines.text: People say Zoro's raw strength would have gotten there anyway.

shot.fallback: strong swordsman swinging at a knight

lines.text: But Sommers heals through raw strength. That's what he's built for.
The loss at the Baratie is the reason Zoro can answer a Knight of God.

shot.fallback: blade piercing a glowing steel heart

lines.text: And that's why I keep saying...

shot.fallback: hawk eyed swordsman with a black blade
